A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ARM and Ada-GRPO. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching analyses that were relocated or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and evaluation results, including Tables 1–2, training dynamics, a decay ablation, and appendix analyses of reflection and overthinking.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds training-data and reasoning-format ablations, GPQA/StrategyQA evaluations, LLaMA experiments, and further L1 comparisons.

M1.justification: Equations 6 and 7 change the stated objective from averaging per-response token means to averaging all tokens within the response group. Appendix H also adds an optional inference procedure that executes generated Code and falls back to simulated output upon failure. The core SFT, diversity reward, decay, and four-format framework remain. The PDFs do not establish whether the objective revision reflects changed implementation or corrected documentation.

E1.justification: v2 adds ARM evaluation on GPQA-Main, GPQA-Diamond, and StrategyQA, plus an AIME 1983–2024-only training condition. Table 11 additionally includes AMC and olympiad_bench in the L1 budget analysis. These expand task and training-data coverage while retaining the original training datasets and seven main evaluation benchmarks.

E2.justification: L1, previously compared with ARM only on CSQA in Figure 4, is additionally compared on the retained OBQA, GSM8K, MATH, SVAMP, BBH, and AIME’25 tasks in Table 12. The main Table 1 comparator roster and the existing THINKPRUNE comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include inference-time exclusion of selected reasoning formats, a LLaMA-3.2-3B configuration, and L1 budget sweeps at 512, 1024, 2048, and 3600 tokens. Appendix K.3 adds a separate comparison using aligned 7B DS-R1-Distill backbones and dataset-specific L1 budgets based on ARM’s token usage. The original main evaluation settings and Appendix D hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of whether biased training data cause format collapse (Tables 4–5), whether interpreter execution helps (Table 8), and what happens when Direct Answer, Short CoT, or Long CoT is unavailable (Table 9). Table 11 adds token-budget sensitivity analysis. The existing decay, reflective-word, and overthinking analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The reflection analysis remains averaged over eight runs, moving from Appendix E to G. Existing pass@1 and majority@8 reporting is retained, and additional rows use that practice. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or additional seed information that changes the uncertainty-reporting approach.

E6.justification: The original main tables and reflection results are unchanged, but substantial new results cover training bias, additional benchmarks, format ablations, LLaMA, and L1 budgets. For example, Table 6 reports StrategyQA accuracy/tokens of 73.8%/229 for ARM versus 72.9%/646 for GRPO. Table 9 reports AIME’25 accuracy falling from 16.7% to 8.3% when Long CoT is removed. These are added experimental comparisons, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: The objective normalization in Equations 6 and 7 changes from equal weighting of response-level averages to a token-level average across the group. These expressions are not equivalent for unequal response lengths. This is a localized mathematical revision; the reward, decay, advantage definitions, and absence of formal proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: adaptive selection among four formats, Ada-GRPO addressing format collapse, approximately 30% average token savings, approximately twofold training speedup, and three reasoning modes. The new appendix evidence supports these claims without redefining their main scope.

C2.justification: New discussion identifies training-data bias as a cause of format collapse, explains smaller LLaMA savings through repetitive outputs, and discusses execution latency and resource costs. Appendix L adds specific limitations concerning predefined formats and missing hard-task training data. Appendix K expands the budget-estimation argument, although its claim of consistent L1 superiority with similar token usage overstates Table 12.

D1.justification: The original hardware, training frameworks, SFT/RL hyperparameters, and data-processing instructions remain unchanged. v2 supplies implementation information for interpreter execution and fallback, specifies the historical AIME training range and inference-time format exclusions, and identifies the L1-Qwen-7B-Exact checkpoint and budget-setting procedure.

R1.justification: Six references are added: HybridMind, Chain of Code, OctoThinker, and sources for StrategyQA, GPQA, and LLaMA 3. They support the added experiments and implementation discussion. The main related-work organization and positioning around autonomous efficient reasoning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained, with limited copyediting, updated affiliations and venue information, and new appendix cross-references. New appendix sections accompany the added studies; the existing reflection, overthinking, and length-penalty sections are renumbered or expanded. There is no extensive rewriting of the main narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds eight substantive result tables, numbered 4–6 and 8–12, displaying training bias, additional benchmarks, format ablations, LLaMA results, and L1 comparisons. Existing figures and original table content are retained; the reflection table becomes Table 7, and Figure 5 moves from page 8 to page 9. The principal visual change is the substantial expansion of tabular evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central design: training-bias and format-removal controls address questions left untested in v1, while GPQA/StrategyQA and LLaMA experiments broaden evidence for generalization. The new limitations also clarify applicability. These gains outweigh localized weaknesses: the loss-normalization revision is unexplained, and Appendix K.3 overstates Table 12, where ARM has lower OBQA accuracy and substantially higher AIME token usage than L1.
